data.why: The app is a pure parameter-entry calculator (sliders/number inputs for dose, fractions, gaps) with a bundled radiobiological library of 34 organs and 20 tumour sites (src/lqlequiv/data/tissues.json); it takes no file uploads.

goals: Compute BED and EQD2 for a multi-fraction treatment schedule to a chosen organ at risk and tumour site
Estimate normal-tissue complication probability (NTCP) and tumour control probability (TCP) for the entered schedule
Quantify how a treatment gap or interruption changes the equivalent dose via accelerated proliferation
Compare a hypofractionated schedule against a conventional one on a common EQD2 scale
Explore the therapeutic window: the fraction size that spares the organ most or delivers the most dose to the target for a fixed effect
Assess sensitivity of the equivalent dose to uncertainty in the alpha/beta ratio

review.summary: The tree captures the calculator's purpose well: equivalent dose, NTCP and TCP for an organ/tumour pair across multi-course schedules, with gaps, twice-daily delivery, α/β sensitivity, isoeffect and therapeutic-window sweeps, and saved scenarios. Every screen I checked supports its node. It needs small fixes before filing: correct or drop the input-style feature (its 'keeps values' claim was refuted), add the cancer-risk output, and tighten a few labels and specifics.
